senses.gloss: c. (b. h.; v. <cite ref="H01220"><he>חָמַר</he> II</cite> a.

units: <cite ref="Shabbat 152a:6">Sabb. 152ᵃ</cite> <he>דעל ח׳ וכ׳</he> he who rides an ass is a freeman.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 143a:8">B. Bath. 143ᵃ</cite> <he>את וח׳</he> thou and the ass (shall own my property, a form of donation implying a rational and an irrational being).—
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 1:2">Bekh. I, 2</cite> <he>ח׳ שילדה וכ׳</he> if an ass gave birth to &c.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 33a:9">Snh. 33ᵃ</cite> <he>הלכה חֲמוֹרְךָ וכ׳</he> thy ass is gone, Tarfon! (I shall have to make compensation for erroneous judgment); a. fr.

senses.gloss: (cmp. various uses of horse) a contrivance for working-men, rest, jack, stocks &c.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 14:3">Kel. XIV, 3</cite> <he>ח׳ של נפחין</he> the smiths’ ass (‘on which the smith sits while using its head as an anvil’, Maim.; ‘the rest of the bellows’, R. S.). Ib. XVIII, 3 <he>וח׳</he> a stand on which the bedstead is placed.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65:22">Gen. R. s. 65</cite>, end <he>ח׳ של חרשים</he> carpenters’ sawing-jack (an instrument for torture); <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70:17">Gen. R. s. 70</cite> (alluding to <cite ref="Proverbs 27:22">Prov. XXVII, 22</cite>) <he>אפי׳ … בח׳ של חרשים וכ׳</he> even if you put the wicked man on a carpenter’s jack, you cannot make anything useful out of him (sufferings will have no effect on him); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 201">Yalk. Kings 201</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 961">Yalk. Prov. 961</cite>; (Pesik. Shek., p. 15ᵃ <he>במכתש</he>).—Pl. <he>חֲמוֹרִים</he>.
Gen. R. s. 75; a. fr.—Denom. חַמָּר, חִמִּר.—Fem. חֲמוֹרָה.
